bio_en: Khachik Aslanian, known as Koriun, Tigran and Anton, was the son of a Trabzon barber, Stepan, who lived among Turks and was thought to be pro-Turkish, yet at fourteen he joined a group of revolutionary youths. In August 1895 the Trabzon committee decided to strike at the official 'commissar' of the coming massacres; Khachik's group carried out the attack on the night of the Sultan's accession anniversary, wounding their targets and escaping in a gunfight with gendarmes. He later joined Armenian-Macedonian revolutionary bands in European Turkey and fell in 1901 near Edirne, where a mixed band had tried to capture the vali; Droshak mourned him in May 1902.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Possibly the 'Khachik' among the terrorists credited to Hovsep Arghutian's Trabzon work (#553) - not confirmed.
